references.text: The Jubilee year is introduced here, where all property must be returned to the original owner, forming the basis for the right of redemption in verse 24.
Explains that the land belongs to the Lord and that the Israelites are merely strangers and guests, which justifies why a right of redemption must be granted for all land.
Elaborates on the practical rules for redeeming land, including the kinsman's right to redeem and the return in the Jubilee year.
Boaz explains the right of redemption (ge'ullah) in practice, where the nearest relative has both the right and obligation to buy back the family's land.
Jeremiah exercises his right of redemption as the nearest relative by purchasing Hanamel's field in Anathoth, in accordance with the law of ge'ullah.
Ezekiel speaks about the inherited land and the people's right to it, referencing the laws concerning property and redemption.
The Levitical cities and pasturelands as an inheritance illustrate the principle of irrevocable ancestral land in Israel.
